title: How's My Job Fit?
description: Compares a candidate's own evidence with a job's requirements and shows what is fully supported, transferable, partial, or not shown at all. Files never leave the browser.
highlights: Parses resumes and notes in the browser (PDF through pdf.js, Word through mammoth, images through Tesseract OCR), so nothing is uploaded or stored

Scores fit with a deterministic weighted model: requirements ranked by importance, eligibility checks kept separate from skills, and transferable evidence given partial credit with the reasoning shown
Ships six fictional example reports across industries plus public methodology and limitations pages, so a reader can judge the method before trusting a score

resume.title: How's My Job Fit? - Evidence-Based Job-Fit Reports
resume.stack: Next.js, React, TypeScript, pdf.js, Tesseract.js, Vercel
bullets: Built a candidate-side job-fit workbench that parses resumes in the browser (PDF, DOCX, OCR) and scores them against a posting with a deterministic weighted model that keeps eligibility separate from skills.
Shipped six fictional example reports and a public methodology page; launched on Vercel in August 2026.

title: SoloMock
description: Talk through a coding problem out loud with an AI interviewer that hears you and watches your editor. Feedback arrives while you are still speaking.
highlights: Built the voice loop on OpenAI's Realtime API over WebRTC. Debounced snapshots of the code editor stream into the model, so the interviewer reacts to what you type as well as what you say
Wrote 15 per-problem interviewer briefs: a solution tree, a four-step hint ladder, follow-ups, and edge cases. The system prompt is built from the brief, so sessions stay consistent
Kept costs bounded with a per-IP rate limit, a 15-minute session cap, short-lived ephemeral keys, and a request-access flow that posts to Discord for manual approval

resume.title: SoloMock - Realtime Voice Mock Interviewer
resume.stack: Next.js, TypeScript, OpenAI Realtime API, WebRTC, Monaco, Tailwind CSS, Vercel
bullets: Built a browser-based mock-interview workspace that combines live voice, a Monaco code editor, and 15 structured problems; streamed debounced code snapshots over a WebRTC data channel so feedback stays in sync with the candidate's work.
Protected sessions with server-minted ephemeral keys, sliding-window rate limits, a 15-minute session cap, and a manual extended-access workflow.

title: Gasolytics — US Gas Price Map
description: Gas prices for all 50 states and DC on one interactive map, with state and metro pages, a trip cost calculator, and an EV-versus-gas comparison.
highlights: Draws the choropleth with d3-geo on the server and ships it as SVG, so no d3 code goes to the browser. Metro price pins, hover tooltips, wheel zoom, drag pan, and a per-state panel

Grew from a map into a toolkit: 51 state pages, metro pages, cheapest-gas-near-me, a trip calculator, an EV suite with per-state registration fees and break-even miles, and gas-tax, border-gap, and affordability pages
Reads daily AAA averages for four fuel grades from a Vercel Blob snapshot feed through an in-process cache. Mobile app-shell layout with a tab bar and a drag sheet over the map

resume.title: Gasolytics - US Gas Price Map
resume.stack: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, d3-geo, Vercel Blob, Vercel
bullets: Built an interactive US gas-price map with a d3-geo choropleth projected to SVG server-side (so no d3 ships to the client), metro price pins, wheel-zoom/drag-pan, and per-state detail panels.

Expanded it into a national fuel-economics toolkit with 51 state pages plus metro pages, a trip-cost calculator, an EV-vs-gas suite, and gas-tax, border-gap, and affordability analyses fed by daily AAA snapshots.

title: SoloYap
description: Spoken English practice with an AI partner. Pick a scenario, talk it through, and get a correction and a better phrasing after every turn.
highlights: Realtime voice over WebRTC on OpenAI's Realtime API. A grammar correction and a better phrasing come back after each learner turn
13 scenarios graded A2 to C1 on the CEFR scale, plus free chat and custom topics, with optional Mandarin and Cantonese hints for beginners
Installable as a PWA, with the same cost controls as SoloMock: per-IP rate limits, session caps, and an email allowlist for extended access

title: Amex Roofing — Site + AI Booking Agent
description: Production website for a Bay Area roofing contractor in English and Chinese: 26 city pages, instant roof estimates from satellite measurements, and an AI chat agent that books onto the crew's calendar.
highlights: Buildless HTML and Tailwind site with English and Chinese homepage twins and 26 city landing pages (13 cities in each language), kept in sync by build scripts

Instant ballpark estimates from Google Solar API roof measurements feed a three-step mobile booking flow. Vercel serverless routes write the appointment to the crew's Google Calendar and post a Discord alert
Hours-aware contact: the crew's phone during working hours, a bilingual AI chat agent after hours, plus SEO articles and a daily analytics digest to Discord

resume.title: Amex Roofing - Client Site with AI Booking Agent
resume.stack: HTML, Tailwind CSS, Vercel Serverless, Google Calendar API, Google Solar API
bullets: Delivered a bilingual (English/Chinese) production site for a roofing contractor with 26 local-SEO city pages and instant estimates from Google Solar API roof measurements.
Built an after-hours AI chat agent and a booking flow that writes appointments straight to the crew's Google Calendar through Vercel serverless routes.

title: Reachspan
description: Marketing site for ReachSpan, a service that runs the website, AI receptionist, reviews, and social listening for local service businesses. Booking a call lands straight on the calendar.
highlights: Single-file HTML and Tailwind landing page with a warm-dark hero, custom display and mono typography, and scroll-reveal motion that respects reduced-motion settings
Vercel serverless routes call the Cal.com API for available slots and bookings, so an audit call is confirmed on the calendar without a form round-trip
Spec demos are labelled as demos. No fabricated results or testimonials anywhere on the page

title: Throughline — Technical Learning Ecosystem
description: The hub that connects six technical guides, SoloMock, and Shipyard into one path: learn to code, pick a specialty, build something, prepare, practice.
highlights: Static Astro hub that lays the whole set out as a five-act ladder and routes readers from the programming on-ramp into a specialty guide, then into building and interview practice
Every guide runs on one shared design system, the guide-kit package, with in-browser code and checkpoint quizzes, and follows the same rule: start from nothing, read top to bottom
Each guide's source is available to read; all of the sites deploy on Vercel

resume.title: Throughline - Technical Learning Platform
bullets: Built an Astro and Docusaurus learning platform that connects six technical guides through a five-stage path, on a shared React and TypeScript design system with navigation, quizzes, and code exercises.

title: all-in-one-URL
description: Short links, QR codes, and barcodes with click and scan analytics, on a FastAPI backend with Postgres and Redis.
highlights: FastAPI backend with PostgreSQL, Redis caching and counter batching, and tiered rate limiting
JWT auth with per-resource ownership that still allows anonymous resources
Two-tier app in Docker Compose, deployed across Vercel, Render, Neon, and Upstash

resume.title: all-in-one-URL - Short URLs, QR Codes & Barcodes
resume.stack: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, React, TypeScript
bullets: Built a FastAPI backend for short URLs, QR codes, and barcodes with per-resource analytics, Redis-backed caching, tiered rate limiting, and JWT auth; containerized with Docker Compose and deployed across Vercel, Render, Neon, and Upstash.

title: Programming Basics
description: An introduction to programming for people who have never written code. The on-ramp the other Throughline guides point to.
highlights: Written for readers with no experience, top to bottom, as the shared entry point to the specialty guides
Interactive Docusaurus course with in-browser code and checkpoint quizzes on the shared guide-kit design system
Source available to read; deployed on Vercel

title: Modern Web Dev Guide
description: A web development course in 17 chapters plus a capstone, with about 700 quiz questions, checkpoints you must pass, and chapters that unlock in order.
highlights: Sampled-quiz engine drawing from a bank of roughly 700 questions, shuffled per session, with progress kept in localStorage
Progressive sidebar locking: a chapter opens only after the previous checkpoint quiz is passed
17 chapters plus a capstone covering foundations, the request lifecycle, the stack, team workflows, AI tooling, and careers

title: Modern AI Guide
description: An AI engineering course in 18 chapters, from how language models actually work to shipping and evaluating production systems, with runnable Python challenges in the browser.
highlights: 18 chapters: model foundations, the project lifecycle, the AI stack, solo, startup, and enterprise workflows, decision frameworks, production patterns, and career paths
Quiz component with per-chapter checkpoints that confirm understanding before the next chapter opens
Docusaurus, MDX, and Mermaid, written to be readable by a beginner and still useful to a working engineer

title: Modern Security Engineer Guide
description: Fourteen chapters of offensive and defensive security, from the attacker's point of view to the job of a security engineer, with quizzes and hands-on code challenges.
highlights: Covers cryptography, application security and the OWASP Top 10, secure SDLC, offensive testing, detection and response, forensics, cloud and identity, governance, and the AI attack surface (prompt injection, the LLM Top 10, red-teaming)
Quiz and CodeChallenge components gate each chapter until the concept is demonstrated; an in-page feedback widget collects corrections
Pairs with the Web Dev and AI guides on the same Docusaurus and MDX setup

title: Modern Cloud Engineer Guide
description: Cloud engineering from first principles in 11 chapters: core services, infrastructure as code, Kubernetes, CI/CD, SRE, and platform engineering.
highlights: 11 chapters: foundations, core services, infrastructure as code, Kubernetes, CI/CD and GitOps, observability and SRE, platform engineering, cloud security, FinOps, MLOps and LLMOps, and career
Interactive Docusaurus course with checkpoint quizzes and Mermaid diagrams on the shared guide-kit design system
Source available to read; deployed on Vercel as part of Throughline

title: Modern Data Engineering Guide
description: How data gets from a raw source to trusted, query-ready tables, in 12 chapters: storage and file formats, SQL engines, modeling, Spark, ingestion and CDC, dbt, orchestration, streaming, and the lakehouse.
highlights: 12 chapters from foundations through storage and formats, SQL and query engines, modeling and warehousing, Spark, ingestion and CDC, dbt, orchestration, Kafka streaming, the lakehouse, data quality and governance, and career

Each topic is taught as a concept first (columnar storage, desired-state pipelines, exactly-once delivery) and then mapped to the current tools: Snowflake, BigQuery, dbt, Airflow, Kafka, Iceberg, and Delta
Built on the shared guide-kit design system with checkpoint quizzes; source available to read; deployed on Vercel

title: Shipyard
description: Build a portfolio-grade project with guidance, then have it graded by Claude against a rubric. The grade explains gaps and next steps instead of passing or failing you.
highlights: Guided build flow that walks a learner through shipping a real project, then grades the result with an LLM-as-judge rubric
The coaching loop explains what is missing and what to do next rather than returning a score alone
The Build act of the Throughline ladder; source available to read; deployed on Vercel

title: SWE Interview Guide
description: Interview prep from zero in 108 lessons over 17 phases, including the newer rounds: AI-assisted coding, problem decomposition, RAG, and agent and eval design. Built alongside SoloMock.
highlights: 108 lessons over 17 phases: foundations through dynamic programming, system design, the AI-era rounds, AI product engineering, frontend, and behavioral
Quiz-gated progression with star ratings, a mock interview timer with phase coaching, and a problem tracker saved to localStorage
One HTML file with JavaScript and Tailwind from a CDN, a hash router, and no build step, served from Vercel

title: 2026 Skills Roadmap
description: A single-page roadmap from zero to a working web development stack: 13 stages across JavaScript, HTML and CSS, the browser, Git, TypeScript, React, Tailwind, and the toolchain.
highlights: 13 stages, numbered 0 to 12, each with a time budget, references, and a concrete deliverable
One self-contained HTML file with a sticky sidebar and dark-mode design tokens
Published on GitHub Pages with no build step

title: Plugrade
description: Trust index for Claude Code plugins: security audits with file-and-line evidence, plus a daily record of what the official directory ships and how installs move.
highlights: Built the daily snapshotter (Playwright on GitHub Actions) that records install counts for 300+ plugins from claude.com/plugins into a Neon Postgres time series. It has run every day since July 31, 2026

Made the scrape refuse bad data. A run only commits if row counts stay in bounds, nearly every row has a count, yesterday's slugs are still present, and no count drops more than 20% in a day. A failed gate keeps the last good snapshot and opens an issue
Wrote the audit publishing pipeline with a default-deny embargo, so an unpublished finding can never be reached by URL. A test pins the rule and fails if the old default comes back
